newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil prices steady in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil prices steady in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Fuel oil markets in north-west Europe were subdued on Monday with little business to shift prices, traders said.
High sulphur barges were unusually quiet, although there was moderate bunker interest.
Trade was heard at $82.50 fob ARA and $81.50 for rmh material, $1 off Friday's values.
"Its sleepier than normal for a Monday," said one trader.
In northern Europe high sulphur buyers were again on the sidelines, looking to better last week's cargo deal for May delivery at $80 cif.
"There is still more to give on price. We've summer weather and summer demand levels come in early and I can't see what's supporting values," said a buyer at a utility.
Buyers looking for keener pricing were heartened by Friday's high sulphur cargo deal from Cartagena to an Italian trader for $79 fob, a number described as low by traders.
Low sulphur was again quiet and well-supplied with swaps dropping $1 to $87/$88 for April. Physical values were said still weighed down by weakness in straight-run and VGO prices.
A co-cargo of low and high sulphur VGO was heard traded from Scandinavia to joint buyers in Europe on Friday.
That was on a part quotes-related/part fixed price deal.
Low sulphur barges were steady at the $91/$92 fob they slipped to on Friday.
